name: Mental Health Checklist
description: Daily and weekly self-care habits to support and protect your mental wellbeing.

items.text: Aim for a consistent sleep and wake time
Eat regular, balanced meals and stay hydrated
items.note: Skipping meals can quietly affect mood and concentration.

items.text: Move your body in a way that feels good for you
Get outside for daylight and fresh air
Limit alcohol and other things that can lower your mood
Rest when you need it without guilt
Pause and name how you are feeling today
Notice your mood without judging it as good or bad
Write down what is on your mind or weighing on you
Acknowledge small wins and things that went okay
Be kind to yourself on harder days
items.note: Speak to yourself as you would to a friend.

items.text: Notice early warning signs that you may be struggling
Take short breaks during a busy or demanding day
Practice slow breathing or a brief grounding exercise
Spend a few minutes on mindfulness or quiet time
Break large worries or tasks into smaller steps
Set realistic expectations and let go of perfection
Limit news and social media when it feels overwhelming
Reach out to someone you trust, even with a short message
Spend time with people who make you feel supported
Talk about how you are really doing with someone safe
Ask for help when you need it
items.note: Sharing how you feel can ease the weight of carrying it alone.

items.text: Set gentle boundaries to protect your energy
Avoid isolating yourself when you are struggling
Make time for a hobby or activity you enjoy
Spend a little time in nature when you can
Do something creative, playful, or just for fun
Listen to music or something that lifts your mood
Allow yourself genuine downtime to recharge
Plan something small to look forward to
Reflect on how your mood has been over the week
Notice what helped and what drained you
Adjust one routine or boundary for next week
Catch up with someone you care about
Consider speaking to a professional if you have struggled for a while
Important: This checklist is general self-care information, not medical advice. If you are struggling, please reach out to a doctor or a qualified mental-health professional.

faq.q: What daily habits support good mental health?
faq.a: The basics make a big difference: regular sleep, balanced meals, water, some movement, daylight, and connecting with others. Adding brief moments of rest, mindfulness, and doing things you enjoy helps protect your mood and resilience over time.

faq.q: Is this mental health checklist medical advice?
faq.a: No. This is general self-care information only and is not a substitute for professional advice, diagnosis, or treatment. If you are struggling with your mental health, please speak with a doctor or a qualified mental-health professional.

faq.q: When should I reach out for professional help?
faq.a: Consider reaching out if low mood, anxiety, or stress lasts for weeks, gets worse, or affects your sleep, work, relationships, or daily life. A doctor or mental-health professional can listen, help you understand what is happening, and discuss options. Asking for help is a strength.

faq.q: How is this different from therapy?
faq.a: A checklist supports everyday wellbeing and healthy routines, but it cannot replace personalized care. Therapy and other professional support offer tailored help for what you are going through. Use this alongside, not instead of, support from qualified professionals.

faq.q: Can I print this mental health checklist?
faq.a: Yes. This checklist is free to print and download as a PDF. Keep it somewhere visible or on your phone so you can check in with yourself regularly and keep supportive habits front of mind.
